input.question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick
input.ground_truth: Because it can. Moving from extreme temperatures one to another can weaken your immune system and that makes it easier for you to get sick. So while it won't directly make you sick to be out in the cold, going between temps is what will do it. Unless it's something like hypothermia. That can make you sick just from being out in the cold.

Question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a little army of germs inside your body that can sometimes make you sick, like tiny bugs. When you are cold, your body works hard to stay warm, but it can’t fight the little bugs as well. 

When you go outside in very cold weather or swim in cold water, your body gets even colder. This makes it a little harder for your body to fight off those tiny sick bugs. But actually, just being cold doesn’t make you sick by itself. It’s more like the cold helps those tiny bugs sneak in and make you feel yucky.

So, people think being cold makes you sick because it’s easier to catch a cold when you are shivery and chilly! But really, the cold doesn’t put the bug inside you—it just makes it easier for the bug to make you sick if you already have it.
